claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially stabilized as a high-temperature BCC phase.
Intermediate-temperature annealing will induce diffusion-mediated compositional segregation in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
The annealing-induced segregation will produce regions enriched in Al.
Segregation may also produce local changes in the Co, Fe, and Ni ratios.
Local compositional deviations destabilize the BCC lattice thermodynamically.
Al-enriched regions facilitate nucleation of a secondary ordered phase.
The secondary ordered phase could have a B2 or L1₂ structure.
The free-energy reduction associated with atomic ordering supplies the driving force for nucleation and growth of the secondary phase.
Kinetic barriers and sluggish multicomponent-alloy kinetics retard completion of the transformation.
Annealed samples will contain a secondary ordered phase alongside a residual BCC matrix.
Secondary-phase formation will produce additional XRD diffraction peaks.
TEM and EDS will reveal distinct precipitates associated with local Al enrichment in annealed samples.
Rapid quenching from the high-temperature state will preserve a homogeneous BCC structure without significant segregation or secondary-phase formation.
The proposed transformation requires an intermediate temperature high enough for measurable diffusion but below the BCC thermal-stability regime.
At sufficiently high temperature, thermal stabilization will retain the BCC phase.
At sufficiently low temperature, diffusion will be too slow to produce the proposed segregation and transformation.
Secondary-phase identity and transformation kinetics may depend on slight composition changes, grain size, and residual strain.
